This file is a summary of the first two pages of the United States Constitution, detailing its structure and key powers. Main Points: • Legislative Structure (Pages 1–2): The U.S. Congress is bicameral, composed of the Senate and House of Representatives; representatives are apportioned by population, while senators serve six-year terms. The House has sole power to impeach, and the Senate holds exclusive authority over impeachment trials with a two-thirds majority requirement for conviction. Both houses can determine their own rules, punish disorderly behavior, and expel representatives with two-thirds concurrence [1]. • Legislative Process (Pages 3–4): A bill must be presented to the President; signing it makes law, or returning objections requiring a two-thirds vote in both houses before becoming law. If the President does not act within ten days (excluding Sundays), the bill becomes law automatically unless Congress adjourns during that period [2]. • Executive Powers and Judicial Structure (Pages 5–6): The Constitution establishes a single supreme court with appellate jurisdiction over cases involving ambassadors, public ministers, consuls, maritime disputes, and state/citizen controversies. It grants the President Commander-in-Chief status, authority to appoint judges and officers with Senate approval, though inferior officials may be appointed by the President alone or via courts [3]. • Treason and State Relations (Pages 7–9): Treason is defined as levying war against the nation, adhering to its enemies, or providing them aid and comfort; conviction requires two witnesses or an open confession. Congress has power to declare treason penalties but cannot attainder citizens without limiting corruption of blood [4]. The Constitution also mandates that each State respect public records from other states while Congress regulates proof methods [4]. Summary of all 9 pages.
